summary: Mount Elwell lookout, Plumas NF: built circa 1915 (sources disagree), staffed through the 1920s, replaced by Mills Peak in 1932-34; removed after 1933, roof remnants at the summit.

facts.design: Small observation cabin, about 8 by 8 feet, reportedly of galvanized iron
facts.status_note: Removed after 1933; remnants of the metal roof are reported clinging to boulders at the summit

staffing.status: replaced as the primary fire-detection site by Mills Peak

access.note: Hiking route from the Lakes Basin campground, described as the most strenuous hike in the area

visit.trail_note: About three miles and roughly 1,500 feet of climb from the Lakes Basin campground, per the Lakes Basin guide.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest

events.note: Register description says constructed circa 1915; the Built field says circa 1918; a 1916 newspaper places a station there
Earliest staffing record in these sources: a man employed through the summer at the government lookout station
Daniel Morehead, of Belden, entered duties as lookout in June 1923
Lookout McCullough struck by lightning while at the telephone
Victor R. Hake phoned in a fire report from the station
Mills Peak lookout took over as primary fire-detection site; register says 1933/34, Lakes Basin guide says 1932, Mills Peak register says first lookout built 1933

corrections.proposed: built circa 1915 (register Built field says circa 1918)
corrections.why: The register's own description says constructed circa 1915, and a 1916 newspaper places a summer worker at the station, which is hard to square with 1918.
The register says removal came 'sometime later' and gives the removal date as 'After 1933', so 1933 is not the removal year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register Built field says circa 1918, the register description says circa 1915, a 1916 newspaper places a summer worker at the station, and a Lakes Basin guide says 1910. Story gives circa 1915 with the disagreement stated.
Register says Mills Peak replaced Elwell in 1933/34; the Lakes Basin guide says 1932; the Mills Peak register says the first Mills Peak lookout was constructed in 1933. Story gives all of them.

sources.title: Mount Ewell - Forest Lookouts (newspaper clippings compilation)

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1918 built date conflicts with the register's own description (circa 1915) and with a 1916 newspaper; the story gives circa 1915 and states the disagreement. The Lakes Basin page is a commercial lodge's guide (the lodge operates under a Forest Service permit); it is used only for the 1910 and 1932 dates and for what remains at the summit. The Hake PDF is a two-column scan; the quote 'the last to serve on Mt. Elwell and the' is a single line from the cached text. Staffing after 1936 is not documented here, so the story stops at the 1930s. Morehead's June 1923 start and the May 1924 'third year' notice do not form one run of seasons, so the story gives them separately. The Hake sentence is split across two evidence entries because the PDF columns interleave.
